newsitem.title: USA: Calif. new businesses up 3.9 pct from 1995-report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. new businesses up 3.9 pct from 1995-report.

text.p: The number of new businesses incorporated in California in 1996 rose nearly four percent from 1995 levels, reflecting the state's growing economy, according to a report on Tuesday.

An total of 48,301 new incorporations were registered with the Secretary of State's office in 1996, up 3.9 percent from 46,499 for 1995, and up 18.1 percent from 40,900 in 1991, Santa Ana-based CDB Infotek said.

"All the elements are in place for continued business growth on into 1997. In fact, if current trends stay in place, the number of California incorporations could pass 50,000 for the first time this decade," Rick Rozar, CDB Infotek's president, said in a statement.

The increase in the number of new businesses was strongest in the San Francisco Bay area. In Santa Clara County, the year-over-year increase was 11.5 percent. In San Francisco County the number was up 10.7 percent.
At the other end of the scale, most rural areas saw little or no growth in new businesses, CDB Infotek, a public records information service, said.
